name: Coolify
tagline: Self-hostable PaaS — an open-source Heroku/Vercel alternative.
description: Coolify turns any server into your own application platform: git-push deployments, one-click databases, automatic SSL and managed cron, all through a clean UI. Everything runs on hardware you control, so no platform can rate-limit, reprice, or shut down your stack.
dockerCompose:
# Minimal dev setup — for production use the official install script:
# curl -fsSL https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/install.sh | bash
services:
  coolify:
    image: 'ghcr.io/coollabsio/coolify:latest'
    restart: always
    container_name: coolify
    ports:
      - '8000:8080'
    env_file:
      - .env
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ~/.coolify:/data
    depends_on:
      - postgres
      - redis
  postgres:
    image: 'postgres:16-alpine'
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE:-coolify}
    volumes:
      - coolify-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  redis:
    image: 'redis:7-alpine'
    restart: always
    volumes:
      - coolify-redis:/data
volumes:
  coolify-db:
  coolify-redis:

independence.dataFormat: App definitions and configs live in your own PostgreSQL instance and Docker; exportable and migratable at will.
independence.telemetry: Anonymous telemetry exists but can be disabled in settings; no data leaves your server otherwise.
independence.offline: Runs entirely on your server; works on machines with no inbound cloud dependency.

name: Uptime Kuma
tagline: Self-hosted monitoring with a polished status page.
description: Uptime Kuma monitors HTTP(s), TCP, DNS, Docker containers and more, with alerting to Slack, Discord, Telegram, email and dozens of other channels. A single container, a single SQLite file — your uptime history is yours, not a SaaS dashboard you rent.
dockerCompose:
services:
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '3001:3001'
    volumes:
      - uptime-kuma-data:/app/data
volumes:
  uptime-kuma-data:

independence.dataFormat: All monitors and history in one SQLite file under /app/data — copy it and you have migrated.
independence.telemetry: None. Metrics never leave your instance.
independence.offline: Runs fully offline; monitoring itself obviously needs network access.

name: Vaultwarden
description: Vaultwarden implements the Bitwarden server API in a single lightweight container, working with every official Bitwarden client. Your vault stays encrypted end-to-end on hardware you own — the cloud never sees your secrets.
dockerCompose:
services:
  vaultwarden:
    image: vaultwarden/server:latest
    container_name: vaultwarden
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DOMAIN: https://vaultwarden.example.com
    ports:
      - '80:80'
    volumes:
      - ./vw-data:/data

independence.dataFormat: Bitwarden's open, client-side-encrypted vault format; export to JSON at any time.
independence.offline: Official Bitwarden apps cache your vault offline and sync when the server is reachable.

name: Authentik
tagline: Self-hosted identity provider — SSO, SAML, OIDC, LDAP.
description: Authentik is a full identity provider: single sign-on, MFA, user federation, outbound/inbound SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning and a flexible policy engine. Replace per-app logins with one provider you administer, on infrastructure you own.
dockerCompose:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: authentik
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${PG_PASS:?database password required}
      POSTGRES_DB: authentik
    volumes:
      - authentik-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U authentik']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
  server:
    image: ghcr.io/goauthentik/server:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: server
    environment: &authentik-env
      AUTHENTIK_REDIS__HOST: redis
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__HOST: postgres
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__USER: authentik
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__NAME: authentik
      AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD: ${PG_PASS}
      AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY: ${AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY:?generate with openssl rand -base64 60}
    ports:
      - '9000:9000'
      - '9443:9443'
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
  worker:
    image: ghcr.io/goauthentik/server:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: worker
    environment: *authentik-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
volumes:
  authentik-db:

independence.dataFormat: Users, groups and flows in your PostgreSQL; standard protocols (SAML2, OIDC, SCIM, LDAP) mean zero lock-in downstream.
independence.offline: Fully self-hosted; authentication works with no external identity service.

name: MinIO
tagline: S3-compatible object storage you can run anywhere.
description: MinIO exposes an S3-compatible API over plain storage you control, with versioning, encryption and Prometheus metrics built in. Point any S3 SDK or backup tool at it and drop the cloud-object-storage bill and data-egress lock-in.
dockerCompose:
services:
  minio:
    image: minio/minio:latest
    container_name: minio
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER:?set a root user}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:?set a strong password}
    ports:
      - '9000:9000'
      - '9001:9001'
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

independence.dataFormat: Speaks the S3 API — the industry standard — so clients swap by changing an endpoint URL. Objects are plain files on disk.
independence.telemetry: Metrics exposed only to your own Prometheus.

name: AppFlowy
description: AppFlowy gives you docs, kanban boards, tables and calendars in a local-first app — your notes live in open formats on your device, with optional end-to-end-encrypted sync you can self-host. Productivity without handing your knowledge base to a vendor.

independence.dataFormat: Local-first: workspace data is stored on your device in open formats; cloud sync is optional and self-hostable (AppFlowy Cloud).
independence.offline: A desktop/mobile app that works fully offline.

name: Ollama
tagline: Run large language models locally, one command.
description: Ollama bundles model management and an OpenAI-compatible local API so you can run Llama, Qwen, Mistral and dozens of other open models on your own hardware. Prompts, documents and completions never leave your machine — the sovereign answer to metered AI APIs.
dockerCompose:
services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '11434:11434'
    volumes:
      - ollama:/root/.ollama
    # NVIDIA GPU passthrough — uncomment:
    # deploy:
    #   resources:
    #     reservations:
    #       devices:
    #         - driver: nvidia
    #           count: all
    #           capabilities: [gpu]
volumes:
  ollama:

independence.dataFormat: Models stored locally in GGUF format; plain files you can back up and move.
independence.offline: Fully offline once models are pulled.

name: Umami
description: Umami is a simple, fast, cookieless analytics engine you host yourself — pageviews, referrers, devices and goals without third-party trackers or data sales. It is the analytics: the data belongs to you and your visitors, not an ad network.
dockerCompose:
services:
  umami:
    image: ghcr.io/umami-software/umami:postgresql-latest
    container_name: umami
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://umami:umami@db:5432/umami
      DATABASE_TYPE: postgresql
      APP_SECRET: ${APP_SECRET:?replace with a random string}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: umami
      POSTGRES_USER: umami
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: umami
    volumes:
      - ./schema.init.postgresql.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/schema.init.postgresql.sql:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U umami']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

independence.dataFormat: All analytics in your own PostgreSQL/MySQL; CSV export built in.
independence.telemetry: It is the telemetry — cookieless, GDPR-friendly, and stored on your server.
independence.offline: Self-contained stack; measured sites must be online (inherent).

name: Infisical
tagline: Open-source secret and config management for teams.
description: Infisical centralizes .env files, API keys and certificates with client-side encryption, identity-bound access, secret rotation and a CI/CD-friendly CLI. Self-host it and your secrets stop being a line item on someone else's cloud.
dockerCompose:
services:
  infisical:
    image: infisical/infisical:latest
    container_name: infisical
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    environment:
      PORT: 3000
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://infisical:${DB_PASSWORD:?set a database password}@db:5432/infisical
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
      ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${ENCRYPTION_KEY:?generate with openssl rand -base64 32}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?generate with openssl rand -base64 32}
      APP_SITE_URL: http://localhost:3000
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: infisical
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: infisical
    volumes:
      - infisical-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
  infisical-db:

independence.dataFormat: Secrets are encrypted client-side (AES-256-GCM) before hitting your PostgreSQL; plain SQL dumps plus your key migrate everything.
independence.telemetry: Anonymous usage events can be disabled via environment flag.
independence.offline: Self-hosted stack; the CLI caches secrets for offline reads.

name: omp
tagline: A coding agent with the IDE wired in.
description: omp (oh-my-pi) is an agentic coding harness for the terminal with the IDE built in: LSP, debugging, 60+ model providers and a full toolset out of the box. It runs locally against providers you choose — including local models — so your agent workflow and session history stay on your machine.

independence.dataFormat: Sessions live on disk in a readable local session format — grep-able, scriptable, yours.
independence.telemetry: No required account; you point it at whichever model provider you trust.
independence.offline: Local binary; works with local models (e.g. via Ollama).

name: Hermes
tagline: Nous Research's desktop AI agent, running on your machine.
description: Hermes Agent is a downloadable desktop app from Nous Research for running AI agent workflows locally with your own model keys. Conversation history and agent state stay on your device, making it a sovereign alternative to hosted AI assistants.

independence.dataFormat: Chats and agent history are stored on-device.
independence.telemetry: Prompts go only to the model endpoints you configure.
independence.offline: Core agent runs locally; inference depends on your chosen backend (local models work).

name: Herdr
tagline: The runtime your coding agents live on.
description: Herdr is an app for running coding agents that you shape by asking — mods reshape the whole interface. Agents live in herdr-core, a small server on your own machine, so terminals and sessions survive app restarts, updates and crashes across every machine you add.

independence.dataFormat: herdr-core keeps terminal and session state on your machine, not in a hosted workspace.
independence.telemetry: Local runtime; no required hosted service.
independence.offline: Local server + TUI; sessions persist offline.

name: Honcho
description: Honcho is open-source memory infrastructure that lets AI agents remember users across sessions and tools — from Claude Code to your own agents. Fully self-hostable via Docker, so the memory layer for your AI lives in your own database, not a vendor's.

independence.dataFormat: Conversation and user-memory data lives in your own Postgres when self-hosted.
independence.offline: Self-hostable via Docker; the hosted cloud is optional.

name: Immich
tagline: Self-hosted Google Photos replacement with mobile auto-upload.
description: Immich backs up photos and videos from your phone to your own server, with face and object search running on your hardware. Your originals stay as plain files on your disk, so leaving is a copy-paste, not a hostage negotiation.

name: Beszel
tagline: Lightweight server monitoring with historical graphs.
description: Beszel monitors CPU, memory, disk, network and temperature across your machines through a tiny agent, with everything stored on your own server. No vendor account, no data leaving your network.
